name: OrderedDataStore
simple: An OrderedDataStore is a special data store that only holds whole numbers and can give them back sorted. That makes it perfect for global leaderboards like 'Top 10 most wins of all time'.
analogy: An OrderedDataStore is like a high-score board at an arcade that automatically keeps everyone's score in order, so you can just read off the top names.
whenToUse: Global leaderboards across every server (most wins, most coins, fastest time).
Any list of whole numbers you want sorted.
Not for whole player saves: it cannot store tables or text, and it has no versions.
where: Server only. Get it with `game:GetService("DataStoreService"):GetOrderedDataStore("Name")`. It also has GetAsync, SetAsync, IncrementAsync, UpdateAsync and RemoveAsync from GlobalDataStore.

terms.data store: Roblox's save system. It keeps information (like coins or levels) even after players leave and servers shut down, and every server of your game shares it.
terms.key: The name you save a value under, like a label on a locker. A common key is `"User_" .. player.UserId`, for example `User_12345`.
terms.value: The thing stored under a key, like a number, text, true/false, or a table.
terms.server: The Roblox computer in charge of one copy of your game. Data stores can only be used from server Scripts.
terms.pcall: Short for 'protected call'. It runs a function and catches any error instead of letting your whole script crash. It gives back `true` plus the results if it worked, or `false` plus the error message if it failed.
terms.async / yield: Functions ending in `Async` talk to Roblox's computers over the internet, so they take a moment. While waiting, your script pauses (yields), then carries on when the answer arrives.
terms.rate limit / budget: How many data store requests a server is allowed to make per minute. For normal reads and writes the default is 60 + 40 for each player, so a server with 10 players can do 460 reads per minute. If you go over, requests are slowed down or dropped.
terms.UserId: A player's permanent ID number. It never changes, even if they change their name, so it makes a great key.
terms.ascending / descending: Ascending means smallest first (1, 2, 3). Descending means biggest first (3, 2, 1). For 'top scores' you want descending.
terms.pages: The sorted list comes back in pages, like a book. Each page holds up to 100 entries.
terms.integer: A whole number, like 7 or -20. Not 7.5.

examples.title: Top 10 most wins
examples.code:
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local winsStore = DataStoreService:GetOrderedDataStore("TotalWins")

-- Give a player a win (IncrementAsync adds to their number)
local function addWin(player)
	pcall(function()
		winsStore:IncrementAsync(tostring(player.UserId), 1)
	end)
end

-- Print the top 10
local function printTop10()
	local ok, pages = pcall(function()
		return winsStore:GetSortedAsync(false, 10) -- false = biggest first
	end)
	if not ok then return end
	for rank, entry in pages:GetCurrentPage() do
		-- entry.key is the key, entry.value is the number
		print(rank .. ". User " .. entry.key .. " - " .. entry.value .. " wins")
	end
end

while true do
	printTop10()
	task.wait(60) -- refresh once a minute, not every frame
end
explain: Each player's key is their UserId as text, and the value is their number of wins.
`GetSortedAsync(false, 10)` asks for one page of 10 entries, biggest first.
We refresh only once a minute because sorted reads have a small budget (about 5 + 2 per player per minute).

gotchas: Values must be whole numbers. Tables, text and decimals will not work.
There are no versions: setting or removing a key replaces it for good.
Sorted reads have a small budget, so refresh leaderboards every minute or so, not constantly.
Only works from server Scripts, and calls should be wrapped in pcall.

OrderedDataStore:GetSortedAsync.simple: Gives back the entries sorted by their number. First value: true for smallest first, false for biggest first. Second: how many per page (up to 100). Optional third and fourth: a minimum and maximum value to filter by.
OrderedDataStore:GetSortedAsync.example:
-- Script in ServerScriptService
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local timeStore = DataStoreService:GetOrderedDataStore("FastestTimes")

-- Smallest times first (fastest runs), only between 1 and 600 seconds
local ok, pages = pcall(function()
	return timeStore:GetSortedAsync(true, 5, 1, 600)
end)
if ok then
	for _, entry in pages:GetCurrentPage() do
		print(entry.key, entry.value)
	end
	if not pages.IsFinished then
		-- pages:AdvanceToNextPageAsync() would load the next 5
	end
end
